acceptance: review-packet --extra-diff <path>=<base> (repeatable) appends that repository's diff base..HEAD, with its changed-path list and HEAD sha, in the same format as configured nested repos; a path outside the project or not a repository top is refused with the next step

A changed path that lies inside a sibling repository (M14.1) is reported once per repository ('in sibling repository <path>, not configured: pass --extra-diff <path>=<base> or configure nested_repos') instead of one 'named in the packet but not at commit' line per file; a test pins both
review_packet.py stays within 400 lines: its argument parser moves to review_packet_args.py. Out of scope: choosing a base automatically for unconfigured siblings
nodes.title: review-packet includes sibling repository diffs

acceptance: The post-run check covers configured nested repos as reconcile does: a changed or untracked path in one is a finding, never 'clean'

For each sibling repository (M14.1), reconcile and the post-run check report its changed and untracked paths (for example an untracked artifacts/ directory) as a warning naming the repository and saying it is not configured, so it is not checked against touch zones; neither reports clean while such paths exist; a test with an untracked directory in a sibling pins both outputs
Out of scope: touch-zone enforcement inside unconfigured siblings, and cleaning anything
nodes.title: worker reconcile and the post-run check see sibling repositories

acceptance: handoff ready refuses to write READY, and review delegate refuses to launch a reviewer, when implementation_gate_error() would refuse finish-this-task for the same branch and zones, printing the same message and next steps; --allow-empty-implementation on handoff ready mirrors finish's flag; a test shows the refusal at ready, before any review record exists

When the zones that match no changed path all lie inside sibling repositories (M14.1), the check reports 'cannot tell: zones <z> are in sibling repository <path>, not configured in nested_repos' instead of 'nothing was implemented', and does not refuse; a test reproduces the reported case (all code in an ignored sibling repo)

validate (and so add-node and edit-node, which run its zone checks) warns when every touch zone of an open leaf lies inside a gitignored directory, naming the leaf, the directory and nested_repos; a test pins it. Out of scope: diffing sibling repositories for this check, and changing finish-this-task's own check
nodes.title: The implementation-zone check runs before a review is spent, and knows about sibling repositories

acceptance: specy-road review rca <ID> --model <id> builds the rca prompt (as prompt --role rca does), runs it on the model's harness with review delegate's retries and backoff, and keeps a RUN-rca-<model>.json/.log record; it refuses a model that is a party to the leaf (rca_parties) and names the eligible ones; registered from review_delegate's add_parser so review_cli gains no subcommand code

When no rostered, available model outside the leaf's parties exists, review rca and handoff status say so and list the ways forward (an off-roster model with --harness, a human analysis recorded as an RCA with escalate_human, or the fix-round budget's deferral from M12.1) instead of repeating 'next, a root-cause analysis'; a run that fails records state skipped with the reason, and status shows it

A harness usage-limit failure (including Cursor's ActionRequiredError) in a reviewer or analyst run is classified as unavailable, not a capacity retry, and is recorded as available: false (with paused_until when the output gives a reset time) in the gitignored roadmap/orchestration.local.yaml overlay, which orchestrate plan already reads; a test with a fake harness output pins the classification and the overlay entry. Out of scope: changing the escalation rules (M14.10)

orchestrate plan and validate warn, per leaf, when its review loop could escalate with no eligible analyst left (every rostered, available model is the leaf's executor or a required reviewer under the rca_parties rule), naming the leaf and the models; the check lives in new specy_road/rca_plan_check.py and orchestrate_plan.py changes only a call line; a test with a two-model roster asserts the warning and a three-model roster asserts none. Prompt size for rca launches is M15.9's
nodes.title: review rca launches the root-cause analyst like review delegate, and says what to do when no analyst is available

acceptance: With `grind.auto_fix: true` (git-workflow.schema.json, default false) the M18.20 loop sends one fix round per blocked commit (a claim's branch tip with a blocking gate-counted review): `worker message --fix-round` to the leaf's resumable worker, else `worker delegate --rework`, under M18.20's zone-reservation rule, and none while a review of that leaf or its worker is running; before dispatch it appends a `fix_round_sent` event carrying the blocked SHA and an operation id, and a restarted loop that finds that event reconciles the round (worker running, READY, moved tip) instead of sending it again

The cap is `policy.max_fix_rounds`, counted as `review status` counts it; `grind.auto_fix: true` with max_fix_rounds unset is a validate error naming both keys and `grind-session` refuses to start with exit 2 naming both; when `review status --json` state is `fix_round_budget_spent` the loop sends no round, appends `<ID>  # parked after <n> fix rounds at <sha>` to work/grind-hold.txt and emits one `parked` event carrying fix_round_budget's `next` and `next_why`, and no `escalated` event

A round counts as done only when the branch tip moved past the blocked commit and READY names the new tip; a worker turn that ends without moving the tip gets no second automatic round for that commit, and the loop emits `fix_round_no_change` once for that commit; when `review status --json` state is `escalated` the loop sends no fix round and emits one `escalated` event with the printed command, launching no analyst (M18.10)

Tests through the public CLI with a stub harness and a fixed clock: a block triggers one round and a second tick at the same commit sends none; a running review and a running worker each defer the round; restarts after dispatch with a running worker, a stale READY, a moved tip without READY and READY at the new tip each send no second round; a spent budget parks the leaf with the hold line and no escalated event; an unchanged tip gives one fix_round_no_change over several ticks; an escalated leaf gives escalated; auto_fix without max_fix_rounds exits 2. Out of scope: the fix-round prompt text (M14.11, M18.15)
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +150, tests about +200
nodes.title: Automatic fix rounds in the unattended loop, capped by the fix-round budget, then parked for a human

acceptance: A version-2 roster entry's `run:` block for claude-code or codex may list `accounts:` (orchestration.schema.json: each {id, dir, weight >= 0}); claude-code launches with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to `dir`; codex keeps its isolated per-profile CODEX_HOME, one per model and account, linking only that account's auth.json and keeping the native sandbox, approval and memory overrides on launch and resume; `accounts` on another harness, a duplicate id or a dir that does not exist is a validate error naming the entry; the roster holds directories only, never credentials

`worker delegate` picks, among accounts with weight > 0 that are not paused, the one with the lowest (launches + 1) / weight, a tie going to the account listed first; it records `account` in the worker record (worker-record.schema.json) and counts launches in work/.workers/account-counts.json under a file lock so concurrent delegates lose no count; weight 0 drains an account (no new sessions); with no usable account it refuses, naming the entry

`worker message` and `worker resume` use the account recorded on the worker; when that account is drained, paused or no longer listed and another usable account exists, they start a fresh session with the same worker id and the original turn prompt on a picked account, bypassing only the old account's paused_by_limit wait, and print one line saying so; with no usable account they refuse and launch nothing

A worker turn that fails with a usage-limit error (M18.10's classification) writes `accounts: {<account id>: {paused_until}}` on that entry's roster patch in the gitignored roadmap/orchestration.local.yaml (the reset time from the output, else one hour later), which orchestration_config.py validates and merges without changing the entry-level available, paused_until and unavailable_until patches; an expired pause is ignored; `worker resume` re-sends that turn once on another usable account; an account pause never sets entry-level `available: false`, and the entry is unavailable to orchestrate assign only while every account with weight > 0 is paused

Tests with stub harness outputs: weights 60/40 over ten sequential delegates give 6 and 4; table rows for an equal-score tie, all weights 0, all paused, an expired pause and a removed account; two delegates released together by a process barrier record two launches; a resume stays on its account; a drained account starts a fresh session elsewhere; a usage-limit failure pauses only that account, keeps an unrelated roster patch, and the re-send uses the other account; all accounts paused makes the entry unavailable; a codex launch whose account dir holds a sentinel config.toml and AGENTS.md uses neither; docs show a two-account entry
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +260, tests about +260
nodes.title: Executor account pools: weighted accounts per roster entry, session-account affinity, and failover on a usage limit

acceptance: A reviewer `channels.cli` (or M16.63 `run:` command) may name `{answer}`, which joins PLACEHOLDERS and substitute_prompt in worker_adapter_parsers.py: specy-road passes a fresh path from answer_scratch outside the checked tree and files that attempt's file as the final answer under review_answer's strict rule; the command's stdout and stderr go to RUN-<model>.log only and are never parsed as the answer, even when they hold a schema-valid one; without `{answer}` today's rule holds, and the native codex, cursor and claude-code reviewer commands are unchanged

The answer file is read only as a regular file in that attempt's scratch directory, opened without following symlinks; a missing, empty or whitespace-only file, a symlink, a directory, an unreadable file, or content that is not exactly one complete schema-valid JSON object is a rerun request that files no review, names the case and quotes the transcript's last 20 lines; the post-run write check still runs before filing, and each attempt gets a fresh path so an earlier attempt's answer is never reused

validate warns, naming the entry and the replacement, for a reviewer command that passes the prompt as text (`<prompt>`) rather than `{prompt}` (Linux caps one argument at 128 KiB) and for a codex reviewer command run with `workspace-write` (its Linux sandbox writes mount points that the post-run write check refuses); docs/orchestration-reviewer-output.md documents `{answer}` with one wrapper example per CLI (codex with `-o {answer}`; cursor and claude writing their last JSON object to `{answer}` and printing the rest)

Tests through `review delegate` with a stub CLI: a wrapper that narrates and writes a valid answer file files the record; missing, whitespace-only, prose-wrapped JSON, two objects, an array, schema-invalid, deeply nested and symlinked answer files each file no record and give a rerun quoting the transcript tail; an empty answer file with a schema-valid approve on stdout files nothing; a retry whose second attempt writes nothing files nothing; a `<prompt>` reviewer entry and a workspace-write codex entry each get one warning
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +120, tests about +160
nodes.title: A channels.cli reviewer writes its final answer to a file specy-road names, and its transcript is kept beside the run record

acceptance: `grind.append_only` (git-workflow.schema.json: a list of repo-relative file paths, default empty; the project template and sr/roadmap/git-workflow.yaml list CHANGELOG.md) names files that leaves only add lines to; one rule in shared_zones.py makes a zone equal to an append-only path overlap nothing, and every overlap reader that calls shared_zones (grind-session --plan's parallel batches, validate's registry overlap warning, the M18.20 scheduler) gets it; a directory zone that contains the path still overlaps as today

One pure-additions classifier, shared by review_gate_ready.trial_merge and finish's deterministic resolver (finish_land_deterministic.py), treats an append-only path as resolvable when both sides only added lines relative to the merge base: trial_merge leaves it out of code_conflicts, so review status and M18.24's review run do not refuse it, and finish keeps the integration side's added lines followed by the branch's and completes the merge; when either side deleted or changed a base line the path stays a code conflict and finish refuses as today, naming the file, with refs and worktrees unchanged
validate notices an append-only entry that is a directory or matches no tracked file, naming it

Tests through `grind-session --plan`, validate and the public finish CLI: two leaves zoning CHANGELOG.md fall in one parallel batch, validate's overlap warning agrees, and a directory zone containing it still overlaps; two branches each adding an entry under the same heading, the second not containing the first's landing, land in turn with both entries kept integration side first and the base lines byte-identical, and the second's trial merge reports no code conflict; integration-side replacement, integration-side deletion, branch-side replacement, branch-side deletion, and an append-only conflict mixed with an ordinary-file conflict each refuse with refs and worktrees unchanged; a directory entry gets the notice
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +130, tests about +180
nodes.title: Append-only zone paths such as CHANGELOG.md do not serialize leaves, and finish merges their added lines
